recipe.name: Kimchi Fried Rice
steps: Rinse rice and cook with water, covered, for 15 minutes; rest 10 minutes, then spread to cool.
Pat tofu dry, cube it and fry in half the oil for 6 minutes until golden; remove.
Chop kimchi and spring onions. Heat remaining oil; fry garlic, onion whites and kimchi for 4 minutes.
Add rice, gochujang, soy sauce and tofu; toss over high heat for 3 minutes. Finish with sesame oil, seeds and onion greens.
tips: Use vegan kimchi and vegetarian gochujang; cool rice promptly and refrigerate if preparing ahead.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Vegetable Bibimbap
steps: Rinse rice, add water and simmer covered for 15 minutes; rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Slice vegetables and cube tofu. Divide oil and garlic among separate batches; sauté carrots, zucchini, mushrooms and tofu until tender or golden.
Wilt spinach in the pan for 2 minutes. Season vegetables with soy sauce; mix gochujang, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil.
Divide warm rice between bowls, arrange vegetables and tofu separately on top, add sesame and sauce, then mix before eating.
tips: Cook vegetables separately so each retains its colour and texture.

recipe.name: Vegetable Kimbap
steps: Cook rinsed rice with water, covered, for 15 minutes; rest 10 minutes. Fold in half the sesame oil and salt; cool until warm.
Cut tofu, carrot and cucumber into long strips. Pan-fry tofu and carrot in oil for 5 minutes; glaze tofu with soy sauce.
Blanch spinach for 1 minute, cool and squeeze dry. Lay nori shiny side down; spread thin rice, leaving a clear top edge.
Line fillings across the rice and roll firmly with a mat. Brush with remaining sesame oil, sprinkle sesame and slice with a damp sharp knife.
tips: Keep fillings dry and serve the rolls soon after assembling so the nori stays pleasant.

recipe.name: Vegetable Ramen
steps: Slice mushrooms and carrot, cube tofu and mince ginger and garlic. Heat sesame oil and sauté aromatics for 1 minute.
Add mushrooms and carrot; cook 4 minutes. Pour in stock and soy sauce, add tofu and simmer for 8 minutes.
Cook noodles separately in boiling water according to the packet; drain. Wilt spinach in the broth for 1 minute.
Turn off heat. Dissolve miso in a ladle of broth and stir back in. Divide noodles and broth among bowls; garnish with spring onions and sesame.
tips: Use vegetable-only stock and miso; add noodles just before serving so they do not soften excessively.

recipe.name: Japchae
steps: Boil sweet-potato noodles according to the packet until chewy and tender; drain, rinse briefly and cut into manageable lengths.
Cut carrot, pepper, onion and mushrooms into thin strips. Stir-fry in oil for 5 minutes until just tender.
Add minced garlic and spinach; stir for 2 minutes until wilted. Mix soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil in a bowl.
Add drained noodles and sauce to the vegetables. Toss gently for 2 minutes until glossy; sprinkle sesame and serve warm.
tips: Use sweet-potato starch noodles for japchae's characteristic springy texture.

recipe.name: Kimchi Pancake
steps: Chop kimchi and spring onions finely. Reserve any kimchi liquid and count it within the measured water.
Whisk flour, rice flour and water into a loose batter. Fold in kimchi and spring onions without overmixing.
Heat an oiled nonstick pan. Spread batter thinly and cook each pancake for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and cooked through.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, sesame and sugar for dipping. Cut pancakes into wedges and serve immediately with the sauce.
tips: Choose tangy vegan kimchi and keep the pancake thin for a crisp edge.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Korean Corn Cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Drain corn thoroughly and finely chop onion and spring onions.
Melt butter in an oven-safe skillet. Sauté onion for 3 minutes, add corn and cook until surface moisture evaporates.
Remove from heat and mix in mayonnaise, sugar, pepper and half the cheese. Spread into an even layer.
Cover with remaining cheese and bake for 8–10 minutes until bubbling and lightly golden. Scatter spring onions and serve hot.
tips: Use egg-free mayonnaise and cheese made with vegetarian rennet.

recipe.name: Vegetarian Sundubu Jjigae
steps: Finely chop onion and garlic; slice mushrooms and zucchini. Heat sesame oil and soften onion for 3 minutes.
Lower heat, add garlic and gochugaru, and stir briefly without burning. Add chopped kimchi and mushrooms; cook 3 minutes.
Add vegetable stock, soy sauce and zucchini. Simmer for 8 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Spoon in large pieces of silken tofu; simmer gently for 4 minutes without vigorous stirring. Finish with spring onions and serve piping hot.
tips: Silken tofu gives the soft texture; firm tofu changes the character of this stew.

steps: Press tofu between clean towels for 15 minutes, then cut into thick slabs. Pat dry and season with salt and pepper.
Mix flour and water into a smooth coating batter. Dip tofu in batter, then press panko firmly onto all surfaces.
Heat oil in a wide pan and shallow-fry tofu for 3–4 minutes on each side until golden and crisp; drain on a rack.
Simmer ketchup, soy sauce, sugar and vinegar for 2 minutes. Slice katsu and serve with sauce and finely shredded cabbage.
tips: Press extra-firm tofu well so the crumb coating adheres; the flour batter replaces the usual egg coating.

recipe.name: Inari Sushi
steps: Cook rinsed rice with water, covered, for 15 minutes; rest 10 minutes off the heat.
Warm vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved. Fold into hot rice with sesame, then fan until lukewarm.
Drain ready-seasoned tofu pouches gently. Open each pocket carefully and shape rice portions to fit without overfilling.
Fill pockets with warm rice using damp hands. Fold openings inward, arrange seam-side down and serve promptly.
tips: Use explicitly vegetarian seasoned pouches; conventional versions may contain seafood stock.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Mapo Tofu
steps: Cube tofu and finely chop mushrooms, garlic and ginger. Mix starch with water into a smooth slurry.
Fry mushrooms in oil for 6 minutes until dry. Add garlic, ginger and doubanjiang; cook gently for 1 minute.
Add stock, soy sauce and tofu; simmer gently for 6 minutes, shaking the pan to avoid breaking tofu.
Stir in slurry and simmer 2 minutes until glossy. Finish with crushed Sichuan pepper and chopped spring onions.
tips: Choose vegetarian doubanjiang and taste before adding extra salt.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Agedashi Tofu
steps: Soak kombu and shiitake in water for 20 minutes. Warm gently, remove kombu before boiling, simmer mushrooms 5 minutes and strain.
Press tofu in towels for 15 minutes, then cut into blocks. Grate radish and ginger separately; squeeze radish dry.
Coat dry tofu with starch. Shallow-fry in hot oil for 3 minutes per side until pale golden; drain on a rack.
Warm strained broth with soy sauce and sugar. Pour around tofu in bowls; top with radish, ginger and spring onions.
tips: Pour broth only just before eating to retain the delicate crust.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Hotteok
steps: Mix both flours, yeast, sugar and salt. Stir in warm water and 10 ml oil to form a soft, sticky dough; knead in the bowl for 5 minutes. Cover and leave in a warm place for 60 minutes, until doubled.
Deflate the dough and rest covered for 15 minutes. Mix brown sugar, walnuts and cinnamon separately for the filling.

Use 10 ml oil to grease your hands and work surface. Divide the dough and filling into 8 portions. Flatten each dough portion into a thick disc, add filling, pull the edges over it and pinch completely shut.

Heat a heavy frying pan over medium-low heat. Use the remaining 30 ml oil across batches. Place parcels seam-side down, cook for 1 minute, turn and gently press into pancakes about 1 cm thick without tearing.
Cook for 2 minutes, turn again, cover and cook for 2 minutes until both sides are golden and the centre is cooked. Rest for 3 minutes before serving so the molten sugar filling is less hot.
tips: Glutinous rice flour adds chew; ordinary rice flour does not behave the same way. Keep the filling away from the dough seam to prevent leaks.
recipe.passiveTime: Allow 75 minutes for rising and resting.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Onigiri
steps: Rinse the rice until the water is nearly clear, then drain well. Put it in a heavy saucepan with the measured cooking water and soak for 30 minutes.

Cover, bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid. Turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes; the grains should be tender with no loose water.
Fluff the rice and let it cool just until comfortable to handle. Chop the umeboshi finely and divide into 8 portions. Cut the nori into 8 strips.

With clean damp hands, spread a little of the measured salt on your palms. Divide rice into 8 portions. Cup each portion, place umeboshi in the centre, cover with rice and gently compress into a triangle without crushing the grains.
Sprinkle sesame over the rice triangles and wrap each with a nori strip just before eating. Serve promptly; cool and refrigerate any portions being kept for later.
tips: Use sticky Japanese short-grain rice and shape it warm. Umeboshi is salty, so use only a light coating of salt on your hands.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Tofu Broccoli Stir-Fry
steps: Dry and cube tofu; cut broccoli into small florets and slice tender stalks. Mince garlic and ginger.
Sear tofu in oil for 7 minutes until golden on several sides; remove. Stir-fry broccoli, garlic and ginger for 3 minutes.
Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, starch and water. Add to the pan with tofu and cover for 3 minutes.
Uncover and toss until sauce clings and broccoli remains tender-crisp. Finish with sesame oil and seeds; serve hot.
tips: Dry tofu thoroughly for good browning and less splattering.

recipe.name: Vegetable Tempura
steps: Slice sweet potato thinly and cut zucchini and pepper into strips. Keep small mushrooms whole; dry all vegetables thoroughly.
Heat oil to 175°C in a deep pan, no more than half full. Combine flours, baking powder and salt.
Add ice-cold water and stir briefly, leaving small lumps. Coat vegetables and fry in small batches for 3–4 minutes until crisp.
Drain on a rack; check sweet potato is tender inside. Combine soy sauce and vinegar as a dip and serve immediately.
tips: The listed frying oil is a bath, not oil absorbed; keep batter cold and avoid overmixing.

steps: Knead flour, half the salt and 140 ml hot water into smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Finely chop vegetables and aromatics. Sauté in sesame oil for 6 minutes until dry; add half the soy and remaining salt, then cool.

recipe.name: Crystal Dumplings
steps: Finely chop vegetables, garlic and ginger. Sauté in sesame oil for 7 minutes until dry; add soy and half the salt, then cool.
Mix starches and remaining salt; stir in freshly boiling water. Cover for 3 minutes, then knead with oil when safe to touch.
Keep dough warm and covered. Divide into 24 balls, press thin circles and enclose small portions of cooled filling carefully.
Space dumplings on perforated parchment in a steamer. Steam for 8–10 minutes until translucent; rest briefly before carefully lifting.

recipe.name: Tofu Bao
steps: Mix flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar and salt. Add the warm dough water and 10 ml oil; knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let rise for 60 minutes or until doubled.
While the dough rises, press tofu between clean towels for 20 minutes, then cut into 16 thick rectangles. Cut cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks and keep chilled.
Coat the dry tofu lightly with cornflour. Heat the 20 ml oil in a nonstick pan and fry tofu in a single layer for 3 minutes per broad side, until crisp and golden; remove to a plate.

Lower the heat and cook garlic and ginger in the same pan for 30 seconds. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar and glaze water; simmer for 2 minutes. Return tofu and turn gently for 1 minute until the reduced glaze clings to it.

Deflate and divide dough into 8 equal balls. Roll each into an oval about 12 cm long and 5 mm thick. Brush the inside surfaces with the reserved 5 ml oil and fold loosely in half. Set each bun on a small piece of baking parchment, cover and proof for 30 minutes until puffy.

Arrange buns with space to expand in a steamer above simmering water, without touching the water. Steam covered for 12 minutes; turn off the heat and wait 3 minutes before opening the lid gradually. Steam in batches if needed.
Gently open the warm buns. Fill each with 2 tofu pieces, cucumber and carrot strips, sharing the remaining glaze across the buns. Serve immediately.
tips: Make the filling during the dough rises, then warm it before filling. Keep glaze thick so it does not soak the buns.

steps: Mix flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar and salt. Add the warm dough water and 10 ml oil; knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let rise for 60 minutes or until doubled.
While the dough rises, wipe the mushrooms clean and slice thickly. Cut cucumber into thin strips and finely slice spring onions, keeping the whites and greens separate.

Heat the 20 ml oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook mushrooms in batches for 6 minutes, turning occasionally until browned and their released moisture has evaporated. Return all mushrooms to the pan.

Add spring onion whites, garlic and ginger; stir for 1 minute. Mix soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, cornflour and sauce water, then pour into the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes until thick and glossy, coating the mushrooms.

Deflate and divide dough into 8 equal balls. Roll each into an oval about 12 cm long and 5 mm thick. Brush the inside surfaces with the reserved 5 ml oil and fold loosely in half. Set each bun on a small piece of baking parchment, cover and proof for 30 minutes until puffy.

Arrange buns with space to expand in a steamer above simmering water, without touching the water. Steam covered for 12 minutes; turn off the heat and wait 3 minutes before opening the lid gradually. Steam in batches if needed.
Open the warm buns carefully and divide the glazed mushrooms among them. Add cucumber strips and spring onion greens; serve immediately while the buns are soft and warm.
tips: Cook the mushrooms until their water evaporates before adding sauce; a wet filling makes the buns soggy.

recipe.name: Paneer Tikka Bowl
steps: Cut paneer into 2.5 cm cubes. Mix 120 g curd, 15 ml oil, ginger, garlic, chilli powder, cumin, coriander powder, garam masala, turmeric, 2 g salt and 15 ml lemon juice. Coat paneer gently and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile rinse rice, drain well and put in a saucepan with the measured water and 3 g salt. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low heat for 12 minutes. Switch off and rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff.

Blend mint, fresh coriander, green chilli, remaining 40 g curd, 1 g salt and 10 ml lemon juice into a thick chutney. Slice onion and dice cucumber and tomato; toss the vegetables with the remaining 10 ml lemon juice.

Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat and brush with the remaining 15 ml oil. Lift paneer from excess marinade and cook in batches for 8 minutes, turning carefully until browned at the edges and hot throughout. Avoid crowding the pan.
Divide rice among 4 bowls. Arrange paneer tikka, onion, cucumber and tomato in distinct sections and spoon mint chutney over one side. Serve while the rice and paneer are warm.
tips: Use thick curd so the coating adheres. Prepare the rice, chutney and salad during marination; prolonged grilling makes paneer tough.

steps: Rinse quinoa thoroughly in a fine sieve and drain. Combine with water and 2 g salt in a saucepan, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Cut paneer into 2 cm cubes and pat dry. Toss with cumin, paprika, 2 g salt and 10 ml oil until evenly coated.
Heat a nonstick pan with 10 ml oil. Sear paneer over medium-high heat for 6 minutes, turning to brown several faces; remove as soon as hot and golden.
Dice cucumber, tomato and bell pepper, discarding the pepper seeds. Chop coriander. Whisk lemon juice with the remaining 15 ml oil, 2 g salt and black pepper.
Divide quinoa among 4 bowls. Top with warm paneer and the diced vegetables, drizzle with the lemon dressing and finish with coriander. Serve immediately.

steps: Bring the measured water to a boil. Add soya chunks and boil for 5 minutes or until completely soft. Drain, rinse under cool water and squeeze firmly in small handfuls to remove trapped water. Halve any large chunks.

Mix curd, ginger, 10 g garlic, chilli powder, cumin, turmeric and salt. Coat the squeezed chunks and let stand for 15 minutes. Add cornflour and rice flour and toss until every chunk has a thick, clinging coating.

Heat 600 ml oil in a small deep saucepan to 175°C, keeping the pan less than half full. Fry the coated chunks in small batches for 4 minutes, turning until crisp and reddish-golden. Let the oil return to temperature between batches.
Lift fried soya onto a wire rack to drain. Pat the curry leaves and slit chillies completely dry before tempering.
Heat the remaining 20 ml oil in a wide pan. Fry the remaining 10 g garlic for 30 seconds, then add curry leaves and green chillies and stir for 30 seconds. Add fried soya and toss for 1 minute.
Switch off the heat, drizzle with lemon juice and toss briefly. Serve immediately as a dry, crisp snack with the fried curry leaves and chillies.
tips: The frying oil quantity is the cooking medium; most remains in the pan. Thorough squeezing gives crisp chunks, while excessive curd or retained water makes the coating slip off.

recipe.name: Soya Seekh Kebab
steps: Cut potato into small pieces and simmer in 500 ml water for 15 minutes until tender; drain, let steam dry and mash. In a separate pan boil soya granules in the remaining 500 ml water for 5 minutes, drain, rinse and squeeze very firmly in a clean cloth.

Dry-roast gram flour over low heat for 4 minutes, stirring until nutty; transfer to a bowl. Finely chop 100 g onion and reserve the remaining 80 g as serving rings. Heat 15 ml oil, cook chopped onion for 5 minutes, then add ginger, garlic and half the green chilli; cook for 1 minute.
Add squeezed soya, garam masala, cumin, chilli powder, amchur and 6 g salt to the onion pan. Stir over medium heat for 4 minutes to drive off moisture; cool until comfortable to handle.

Pulse the soya mixture briefly to a coarse mince. Mix with mashed potato, roasted gram flour, 20 g chopped coriander and 10 ml lemon juice. Knead until cohesive, then shape firmly around metal skewers into 8 even cylinders with no cracks.
Blend mint, remaining 15 g coriander, remaining green chilli, curd, remaining 15 ml lemon juice and 1 g salt into a smooth chutney. Keep chilled while cooking the kebabs.

Heat a ridged grill pan over medium heat. Brush the pan and kebabs with the remaining 25 ml oil across batches. Grill for 10 minutes, rotating gently until browned on all sides and firm enough to lift. Slide off the skewers and serve with onion rings and mint chutney.
tips: The mixture should hold its shape before grilling. If loose, cook it briefly to remove moisture and cool before shaping; do not turn kebabs until their first side has set.

steps: Mix flour with 3 g salt. Add the dough water gradually and knead for 8 minutes to form a firm, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes while preparing the filling and sauce.

Boil soya granules in 700 ml of the boiling water for 5 minutes until soft. Drain, rinse under cool water and squeeze thoroughly in a clean cloth; the soya should be moist but release no water when pressed.

Mince 12 g garlic. Heat 15 ml oil and cook onion for 3 minutes. Add ginger and minced garlic, stir for 1 minute, then add cabbage and cook over medium-high heat for 4 minutes. Add squeezed soya, soy sauce, pepper and 2 g salt; stir for 3 minutes until no liquid remains. Spread on a plate and cool completely.

For the sauce, chop tomatoes and simmer with dried chillies, remaining 8 g garlic and remaining 300 ml boiling water for 12 minutes until soft. Cool briefly, then blend with vinegar, sugar and remaining 2 g salt. Heat 5 ml oil in a small pan, add the blended sauce and simmer for 5 minutes until thick enough for dipping.

Divide the dough into 24 pieces and keep covered. Roll each into a disc about 9 cm wide, making the edges thinner than the centre. Divide the cooled filling among them, leave the edges clear, fold into crescents and pleat and pinch firmly to seal.

Grease steamer trays with the remaining 5 ml oil. Arrange momos with space between them above actively simmering water. Cover and steam in batches for 12 minutes until the wrappers look slightly translucent and no raw dough remains at the pleats; the filling must be steaming hot.
Let momos stand for 1 minute before lifting gently from the tray. Serve hot with the red tomato-chilli dipping sauce on the side.
tips: Keep unused dough covered so the edges stay easy to seal. Cool the filling fully and keep it dry to prevent torn wrappers.
